reasoning_traces.think:
Khora introduces a modular architecture where world-state evolution is decoupled from visual rendering. The STBoard maintains a shared, persistent representation of the environment and agent identities, enabling population scalability. Action-conditioned evolution models each agent's motion deterministically based on actions, while geometry-guided view synthesis projects this shared state into multiple camera views. This design ensures cross-view consistency without retraining, supporting inference-time expansion. The key insight is that consistency resides in the shared state rather than in dense inter-agent interactions. The system assumes a static scene prior G and synchronized training data. Failure modes include latency growth with agent count and lack of quantitative state accuracy metrics. The model is evaluated qualitatively on held-out cases and tested for robustness to agent addition/removal. In GSI, this structure supports Bayesian inference over evolving agent populations. In GSE, it enables tactical simulations with variable agent counts.
